# OMP Session Gateway

> Native integration with stock Oh My Pi (OMP) >=18.1.20. No OMP fork, custom build,
> gateway-specific OMP plugin, or publisher credential. Stable v0.6.0 is published as immutable
> GitHub Latest. Keep using OMP in the terminal; the separate gateway discovers collaboration-enabled
> sessions and opens OMP's own encrypted View/Control client in any modern browser, installable as a PWA where the platform supports it. One-time
> setup requires collab.autoStart, Bun 1.4.0, gateway installation, and TUN-mode Tailscale Serve
> with Funnel disabled. No per-session QR scan or link copy. Community project; not affiliated
> with or endorsed by the Oh My Pi maintainers.

## Supported platforms

- Supported and tested in CI on every change (the stock-OMP canaries run daily): Linux, macOS, and Windows gateway hosts; Chrome and Chromium, Edge through Chromium, Firefox, Safari/WebKit, and Android; iPhone and iPad as a WebKit browser, tested with emulation and no physical Apple device. Supported is not qualified: qualification is the exact hardware matrix below. Lanes: portable-source (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows), browser-core (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, iPhone-class WebKit), browser-notifications (Pixel sizes), windows-service-lifecycle, canary and canary-windows.

## Current qualification boundary

- Stable v0.6.0 (source b39ba822195eb61b27667c3211e816f6e10836fe) was promoted from signed candidate v0.6.0-prealpha.4 with identical runtime bytes. Every qualification lane passed on 2026-09-25 on its first attempt against stock OMP v18.3.0; earlier v0.6.0 candidates did not qualify, and the release ledger records each attempt. No claim for arbitrary builds from main.
- Exact OMP v18.3.0 source: 62bc57be1b03ef0802a33cf7f5f530e534527531. Set only collab.autoStart (off/view/control); start participating sessions with plain omp. The gateway reads OMP discovery and queries each host; OMP does not register with the gateway.
- Debian 13 (trixie) x86-64, Linux 6.12.94+deb13-amd64: 83/83 migration/recovery invariants, stock OMP publication/revocation, persistence, tagged-identity denial/exposure, uninstall and resource teardown.
- Mac14,3 / macOS 26.6.1 arm64: doctor 18/18, rollback 23/23, install/rotation/reboot-to-login persistence, real allowlisted identity and forged-header/exposure checks. Positive allowed-user HTTPS was measured on Mac/Pixel, not the tagged Debian CI caller.
- Windows Server 2025 x86-64, build 26100, on a disposable VM destroyed afterwards: the candidate upgraded published v0.5.3, survived a real reboot and started automatically 103.5 s after interactive logon; doctor 15/18 with only the tagged node's identity, PWA and session checks false; named-pipe publication, View/Control 200, stale generations 409, the Pixel's View and Control, readiness rotation, history-selected rollback and uninstall. The claim is start at interactive logon, not at boot.
- Pixel 10 Pro / Android 17 build CP3A.260905.009 / Chrome 153.0.8010.53: View read-only, Control writable, prompt accepted, return to directory; same-page recovery measured at a 250 ms probe cadence: unlock 6,836 ms (including device wake), Airplane 5,196 ms, Doze 286 ms; all seven forbidden capability sinks detectable and clean.
- Background Web Push on the same Pixel with the installed app closed: Private, Session and Preview delivery on the lock screen in 3.6–4.3 s, one notification each; taps to current Control and View, stale-generation scrub, authoritative clear, permission revocation, lock/resume, Wi-Fi and cellular delivery, Airplane suppression and recovery; ten forbidden sinks clean. Force-stop and Doze outcomes are observed variants, never delivery guarantees.
- Tailscale Serve over tailnet HTTPS only, TUN mode required, Funnel disabled. Fresh relay check: 1,800 seconds (2026-09-25T20:42:40.785Z–21:12:40.785Z), four transitions, final phase live. The 30-minute check replaces eight hours, as for every mainline release; eight-hour endurance was not rerun or claimed, no historical endurance transfers, and residual prolonged-operation risk is accepted. No bounded-memory-growth claim is made.
- Other Windows versions are supported and CI-tested, including a daily canary that drives stock OMP's named pipe through the gateway, but not qualified. Specialized attention and branch/resume, and new media qualification remain unqualified/unadvertised. Seeded-fixture product media is not release-qualification evidence for these lanes. Android radio changes can still wedge Chrome; the proven same-page recoveries do not remove that limit.
- v0.5.3 is the migration/rollback predecessor. It sends every push with a per-session Topic that FCM throttles after a burst, and on Windows it can exit at logon without listening when its private-ACL helper starts slowly. Gateway rollback does not switch OMP.
- In v0.5.0 and earlier, the first visit after a gateway upgrade can navigate a pending launch or an open View/Control page back to the directory: the service worker cannot see that a page is in use because Chromium reports each page's creation URL. The first post-release View/Control smoke failures match this navigation. The v0.5.1 fix never navigates from the worker.
- The v0.6.0 published-byte local/Pixel smoke passed on its first attempt across the upgrade from v0.5.3, against Bun's global stock OMP 18.1.20. The v0.5.3 smoke passed on its first attempt across the upgrade from v0.5.2, against stock OMP 18.3.0.

## Fork-era release history

- v0.3.0 requires its exact patched OMP v18.1.14 and matching historical instructions. Its qualification does not transfer to the mainline architecture.
